newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto files amended petition in supreme court.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto files amended petition in supreme court.

text.p: Ousted Pakistani prime minister Benazir Bhutto filed an amended petition in the Supreme Court on Thursday, challenging her dismissal, one of her lawyers said.
The court refused to accept Bhutto's original petition on Tuesday, saying it contained frivolous and scandalous matter.
It gave Bhutto 14 days to appeal against the rejection of the petition or to file an amended one.

Bhutto's lawyer, Aitzaz Ahsan, said he had filed an amended petition to save time instead of appealing. "Our stand remains unchanged that there is nothing frivolous or scandalous in the petition," he told Reuters.
Ahsan said he had written a letter to the court registrar along with the amended petition to place on record Bhutto's disagreement with the court's rejection of the original.
The first petition's 42 pages contained blistering criticism of Leghari for sacking his former political patron.

"As this petition has been drafted in an argumentative manner...and contains frivolous, unnecessary and scandalous matter, it is not entertainable and is hereby returned," the court said in a statement.
It said references to the president and chief justice should be made in proper language.
Ahsan contended in his letter that the petition had been drafted with due respect, but said he was refiling a modified version, omitting all the passages criticised by the court.

Bhutto's government was the fourth to be ousted by a president in less than nine years. On each occasion, presidents have used controversial powers inserted in Pakistan's constitution by the late military ruler General Zia-ul-Haq.
The Supreme Court restored Nawaz Sharif's government after it was dismissed in 1993.
